title: Build VPC network-hardening Terraform module: SGs, NACLs, private DNS, and enforceable egress policies
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module that standardizes network-level security controls for Redwood Private deployments (VPCs). The module must provide: security group (SG) patterns for workload tiers, subnet-level NACL templates for explicit deny rules, Route53 private hosted zone setup with conditional forwarding, and enforceable egress policy primitives (allowlist, proxy endpoints, or NAT gateway patterns). The module should be cloud-first (AWS), support optional on-prem/VPC-like deployments via flags, and expose inputs for per-customer overrides while providing secure defaults (default-deny egress, no public SSH by default).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module under modules/vpc-network-hardening with README and examples for hosted & private deployments
Default configuration applies deny-by-default egress at subnet-level and SG-level allowlist for service endpoints
Private DNS: creates Route53 private hosted zone + optional conditional forwarder to on-prem DNS (configurable)
NACL templates created and attached to public/private subnets with documented exceptions for control-plane traffic
Egress policy options: allowlist CIDRs, managed proxy endpoint (optional), and NAT gateway pattern selectable via variable
Module includes automated health checks: synthetic egress verification and a terraform smoke-test that validates SG/NACL and DNS resolution
Integration test runs in CI that deploys a small test VPC and verifies reachability rules, DNS resolution, and that outbound-only traffic is restricted per allowlist
Security review completed and security_review_required flag set in module manifest
proposed_solution: Create a single Terraform module that composes smaller internal submodules: sgs, nacls, dns, egress. Each submodule exposes inputs for environment (prod/staging), reserved CIDRs, allowed egress endpoints, and management plane IP ranges. Use security group constructs for workload-to-workload allow (stateful) and NACLs for coarse-grained subnet deny rules (stateless) where explicit deny is required (e.g., block 0.0.0.0:22 on private subnets). For private DNS, create a Route53 private hosted zone bound to the VPC and an optional Route53 Resolver outbound endpoint for forwarding to on-prem. Egress policies will support three modes: strict-allowlist, proxy-endpoint, and default-nat. Include a small Lambda/SSM-based validator that runs in the customer VPC during apply to assert egress behavior and DNS resolution for smoke tests.
tasks: Implement SG patterns and reusable rulesets (Carlos)
Implement NACL templates and attach logic (Carlos)
Private DNS implementation + conditional forwarder (Infra team)
Add egress mode switch and proxy-endpoint helpers (Networking)
